text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Tuesday.

LONDON - British stocks jumped to their highest level in six weeks, encouraged by sharp gains in New York after U.S. economic data showed tame inflation, calming fears the U.S. Federal Reserve would raise short-term interest rates again. The FTSE 100 index added 43.5 points or 0.99 percent to close at 4,433.2.

FRANKFURT - German shares also rose as the market continued to benefit from the stronger dollar, which helps German exporters, and strength on Wall Street. The DAX index rose 20.13 points to 3,383.19, and in after-hours trading surged to 3,425.86.

PARIS - The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 52.61 points or 2.06 percent at 2,602.86, on the back of the friendly U.S. economic data which appeared to lower the risk of an interest rate rise by the Fed next month.
ZURICH - Swiss shares also rallied, hitting a record, with the the Broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) up 33.39 points or 1.1 percent to 3,070.95.
TOKYO - The Tokyo stock market was closed for a holiday and will reopen on Wednesday.
HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks edged lower amid profit-taking in China-related issues after their recent surge. The Hang Seng blue-chip index fell 9.75 points to 12,600.42.

SYDNEY - Broken Hill Proprietary Co.'s plan to close its oldest plant as it revamps its steel operations drove Australian shares to their highest close in over two months, brokers and traders said. The All Ordinaries Index gained 17.4 points to 2,479.1, its highest since Feb. 27.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended strong on heavy volume. The industrial index jumped 45.4 points to 8,451.4, the all-share index added 34.4 points to 7,106.4 but the gold index fell 29.8 points to 1,205.2.
